subject.title: [Bug]: macOS app 'Launch at login' stops sticking / appears to turn itself off after app updates

question: Should the macOS app persist OpenClaw-owned Launch at login intent and re-register the app LaunchAgent after updates when live launchd state drifts?
rationale: Current code treats launchd as the source of truth, while the report asks the app to preserve user intent across bundle replacement; choosing the wrong default could either lose the setting or override a deliberate OS-level disable.

options.title: Persist intent and reconcile drift
options.body: Store an OpenClaw-owned enabled intent and re-register only the app-owned LaunchAgent after startup/update drift, with safeguards for deliberate external disablement.

options.title: Keep launchd authoritative
options.body: Continue deriving the toggle from launchd and update docs/UI expectations so OpenClaw does not restore a login item that macOS reports disabled.

options.title: Wait for live update proof
options.body: Keep this parked until a packaged Sparkle update repro shows whether the plist, launchctl registration, or UI state flips first.

recommendation.title: Persist intent and reconcile drift
recommendation.body: Store an OpenClaw-owned enabled intent and re-register only the app-owned LaunchAgent after startup/update drift, with safeguards for deliberate external disablement.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest available history on the macOS app LaunchAgent and launch-at-login state model.
